farTiles.text: Western degrees in the Gulf, admitted on four calendars months apart

farTiles.name: Australia
farTiles.text: Three-year degrees, published IB conversion, and a calendar that runs backwards

farTiles.name: Canada
farTiles.text: Transparent entry requirements, high fees, and a study permit queue

farTiles.name: China
farTiles.text: The joint-venture universities are the real English-taught route

farTiles.name: Hong Kong
farTiles.text: British-style degrees, published IB requirements, and rising fees

farTiles.name: Japan
farTiles.text: A named minority route, on a calendar built for it

farTiles.name: South Korea
farTiles.text: A separate international track, and an academic year that starts in March

farTiles.name: New Zealand
farTiles.text: One national entrance rule, no central portal, and your IB total is the rank

farTiles.name: Singapore
farTiles.text: Everything in English — and a subsidy that comes with a three-year contract

farTiles.name: United States
farTiles.text: Four years, no fixed major on day one, and a very wide price range
